newsitem.title: UK: Dirty tankers mainly flat, Med Aframaxes edge up.
newsitem.headline: Dirty tankers mainly flat, Med Aframaxes edge up.

text.p: Dirty tanker rates were mainly stable on Thursday but some brokers said the 80,000 tonne cross-Med market was set to rise.
"We expect this market to improve," said an Italian broker, referring to cross-Med 80,000 tonners (Aframaxes).
"There has been fairly good enquiry and a lack of good quality tonnage for early April...The trend is positive," he said. He said Aframaxes were done at W110, up about 2.5 points from Wednesday.

But he was less optimistic about Suezmax (130,000 tonne) vessels. He said there had been reports of vessels fixed below W100, against W105 on Wednesday, although enquiries were continuing to emerge, with Exxon and Petrogal looking for ships.
"I would say the market is a little bit weak although it is a bit early to say and we will have to see at what rate Exxon and Petrogal fix. The market is steady, not improving."
The very large crude carrier (VLCC) sector was steady on most routes, with Mideast/west voyages at W57.5, Mideast/Japan at W67.5 and Mideast/Singapore at W60-62.5.

West Africa/U.S. Gulf and North Sea/U.S. VLCCs were also stable at about W72.5 and W77.5 respectively, while West Africa Suezmaxes were fetching W100 for a modern ship and W97.5 for an older vessel, brokers said.
The inter-U.K./Cont 80,000 tonne market was choppy, with vessels fixed at anywhere between W135 and W145, depending on the type of ship and dates.
Inter-U.K./Cont 25,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes firmed to W205/210 from W200 on good enquiry, especially for March positions, while cross-Med fuel oil was steady at W210, brokers said.
In the Western Hemisphere, 70,000 tonne Caribs/upcoast crude was steady to slightly firmer at W212.5, with 50,000 tonne fuel oil cargoes unchanged at W210.
